questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer will usually continue to move straight.
The trailer will swing to the side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will swing to the side.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing to the side. This can cause a jackknife.

questions.question: Before you start a trip, you should:

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before you start driving, close both the emergency and service line shut-off valves. First, open them to check that air reaches all the brakes on all trailers. Listen for escaping air. Then close both valves before you drive.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, you should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving so fuel reaches the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the brake pedal about 20 times to build pressure, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: To help prevent the vehicle from rolling over, you should:

options.text: Speed up quickly after you stop.
Place the load near the back of the trailer.
Place the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: To lower the risk of a rollover, load cargo as close to the ground as possible. Also take curves and turns slowly.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving away from a hazard is safer than trying to stop. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks that have manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day. This stops oil and water from building up in the air tanks.

questions.question: If ABS is only on one axle:

options.text: It still gives you more control when braking.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If ABS is on only the tractor, only the trailer, or only one axle, you still have better control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: To release a dolly's spring brakes before you connect it to a trailer, you should:

options.text: Use the dolly parking brake control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the dolly parking brake control.
questions.explanation: Use the dolly parking brake control to release spring brakes on a converter dolly. This is the first step when positioning the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: If you unlock the pintle hook before pulling the dolly out from under the rear trailer:

options.text: The tow bar may fly up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tow bar may fly up.
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer. This can cause the tow bar to fly up, which can cause serious injury.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: The same speed as the surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as the surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Before each trip, check for emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid burning flares, and one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, use your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: To release a dolly's air brakes before coupling, you should:

options.text: Remove the dolly parking brake control.

questions.explanation: If a dolly has air brakes, open the air tank petcock to release them. This is the first step when positioning the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: Before positioning a dolly for coupling, release the spring brakes by:

options.text: Using the dolly parking brake control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the dolly parking brake control.
questions.explanation: If a dolly has spring brakes, use the parking brake control to release them. This is the first step when positioning the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: Before a trip, the air lines must not be:
questions.explanation: Check that the dolly is in good condition. Make sure air lines are securely attached to the glad hands with no leaks. They should have enough slack to allow easy turning.

questions.question: Trailers built after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: Trailers and dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: The service air line is attached to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It attaches to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, the ____ trailer is most likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Turn gently and smoothly. A quick turn while pulling trailers is dangerous and increases the risk of the last trailer rolling over.

questions.question: If driving through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:

options.text: Try to stop in the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or moving water if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and debris out of the brake system.

questions.question: The best way to avoid glare from oncoming vehicles at night is to:

options.text: Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, glance to the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.
